I was considering it, but I believe we should wait for the updated specs before proceeding. The original specifications indicate that the VPS may not be cost-effective. Affordable options typically offer 8GB of RAM, 2 processors, and internet speeds not exceeding 300MB up and down. As a public pool operator managing around 40 nodes (8 of your own and 32 from others), the basic VPS service will not suffice.

Currently, the recommended specs for 50 nodes are 64GB of RAM, an i5 processor or better, and 500MB of internet. Obtaining such resources from a VPS provider would significantly outweigh the 1 coin per node per day reward received from hosting a public pool (from delegates). Economically, it would be more viable to simply become a delegate yourself to another pool operator.

That said, @Rob 🌽🦊 mentioned the most recent iteration of the nodes uses fewer resources, so we will just have to see the updated requirements. (edited)
